_note: The Humanity Museum's rooms, in walking order. `span` is the historical range a gallery covers (galleries may overlap slightly — history does). A gallery opens when the canonical timeline reaches its earliest exhibit. Titles and epigraphs are never shown while a gallery is still sealed.

galleries.title: Deep Origins
galleries.epigraph: Before tools, before fire — a body learning to stand.

galleries.title: The First Toolmakers
galleries.epigraph: A struck stone keeps its edge for three million years.

galleries.title: Fire and the Hearth
galleries.epigraph: Light that stays after the sun has gone.

galleries.title: Modern Minds
galleries.epigraph: Beads, pigment, graves — the first signs of meaning.

galleries.title: Ice Age Worlds
galleries.epigraph: Painted walls, sewn clothes, whole continents crossed.

galleries.title: First Farmers
galleries.epigraph: In several places at once, people began to stay.

galleries.title: Cities and Signs
galleries.epigraph: Crowds, walls, and marks that could speak for the dead.

galleries.title: Bronze, Horses and Letters
galleries.epigraph: Metal moved by sea; sound was split into letters.

galleries.title: Iron and Ideas
galleries.epigraph: Coins, roads, proofs — and arguments written down.

galleries.title: Engines of the Classical World
galleries.epigraph: Gears in a shipwreck, paper in a river town.

galleries.title: Connected Worlds
galleries.epigraph: Zero travelled west; the compass pointed everywhere.

galleries.title: Print and Oceans
galleries.epigraph: Every copy identical; every ocean joined.

galleries.title: The Scientific Revolution
galleries.epigraph: Look closer. Measure. Publish. Be proved wrong.

galleries.title: Steam and Industry
galleries.epigraph: Coal became motion, and motion became a city.

galleries.title: Waves, Atoms and Wings
galleries.epigraph: Invisible forces, suddenly in human hands.

galleries.title: The Information Age
galleries.epigraph: Switches smaller than dust, orbits within reach.
